acceptance_scenarios.expected: An incident threatens a critical function but monetary loss is zero; classifier must not suppress legal review.
Affected-customer fraction reaches the historical Article 30 criterion but transaction fraction is below it; disjunctive criterion must be preserved.
Affected-transaction fraction reaches the criterion but customer fraction is below it; no AND-gate is permitted.
Customer or transaction denominator is missing, zero, stale or from another institution; classification is UNKNOWN/ESCALATED, never NOT_SIGNIFICANT.
Service outage duration is unknown and may exceed the Article 30 criterion; preserve potential significance and escalate.
Sensitive/classified data is leaked with no measurable financial loss; monetary-only screening must fail.
An incident may produce reputationally damaging public disclosure without proven monetary loss; preserve separate trigger.
A gross financial gain is offset by a gross loss and netted to zero; criterion evaluation must use legally approved gross basis, not netting.
An unapproved capital denominator or floor calculation is used to activate a monetary incident trigger; quarantine threshold policy.
The 2026 transition deadline is stored as 2025 legal commencement or vice versa; reject temporal conflation.
A new entrant after 2025-01-01 claims the transitional period intended for institutions active at commencement; require institution-specific legal review.
An EMF 2/3 institution crosses a deposit threshold in only one year or has missing annual figures; do not silently activate or exempt full-scope rules.
An EMF affiliate is treated identically to the apex entity without assessing differentiated Article 2 obligations; reject scope conflation.
A regulator notification is recorded as sent without an actual traceable receipt; reject completion and preserve escalation.
A one-week follow-up or one-month summary is measured from incident discovery instead of declaration without approved legal interpretation; flag due-date ambiguity.
A legal rule activation or incident-status change attempts to mutate a posted journal, balance, settlement or liquidity; reject side effect.
A cross-tenant analyst reads another institution's sensitive incident evidence; deny, audit and alert.
Recovery replay generates duplicate regulator notifications or financial postings; enforce separate idempotency and independent reconciliation.
